content.text:
I fixed all three problems you hit. The changes are pushed to [PR 194](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/194), and I'm watching CI to confirm the macOS fix.

**What was wrong:**
- **Slow pages and "Could not load workspace":** Moneo's built-in sign-in service (GoTrue) opened a new database connection for every request. On Windows each new connection is slow, so every page spent about 0.5 s just checking you're signed in. Those connections also sometimes failed outright. That caused the "could not load workspace" error, the AI chat not opening, and pages jumping back to where you were.
- **Going back to the website:** after connecting Enable Banking, Scalable or ChatGPT in your browser, you stayed on `localhost:47300` in the browser instead of returning to the app.
- **macOS build failing in CI:** a database add-on was saved under the wrong file name for macOS, so the data service couldn't connect.

**What changed:**
- **Speed:** the sign-in service now keeps its connections open. The check takes about 5 ms instead of about 450 ms. In the packaged app, pages now open in about 0.2 s (slowest 0.3 s); before, each took about 1 s.
- **Errors:** if the sign-in service has a hiccup, the page now offers a retry instead of sending you to the "could not sign you in" page.
- **Sign-ins:** when a bank, Scalable or ChatGPT sign-in finishes, the result opens in the Moneo app window and brings it to the front. The browser tab just says "Continue in Moneo".
- **Security:** the browser can't trigger that hand-off itself. It goes through a private local address that changes every launch and refuses browser requests.
- **Website version:** if you run Moneo from the code, it behaves as before. The app and website share the same code, so other changes reach both.

**Testing on Windows:**
- The packaged app passes all 27 smoke checks and all 16 checks in the full walkthrough test.
- I added two checks to that walkthrough: every section opens twice without errors, and a sign-in result opens in the app window.
- Lint and type checks pass.
- In the full unit test run, 1,547 tests pass and 4 timed out. Those 4 time out only under the full run's load on this machine and pass when run alone. CI on Linux runs them too.

**Not yet verified:**
- The macOS fix, until CI finishes.
- A real bank, Scalable or ChatGPT sign-in from start to finish. The tests use fake ones so they don't cost money or use up your bank's daily limit.
- Code signing and publishing a release. Nothing has been published or merged.

To pick up the speed fix, install the new build and restart Moneo. Your existing data is kept.

content.text:
I found and fixed the cause of "This page couldn't load", and Moneo is open again with the fix and all your data. Good to hear the bank connection now returns to the app properly.

**Why it happened:** the desktop app has a small internal relay (the gateway) between the app and its data service (PostgREST). PostgREST quietly closes connections that have been unused for 30–60 seconds. Sometimes the gateway sent your next page's request down one of those closed connections, and that request failed. That's why it showed up rarely, mostly when Moneo had been sitting for a while, and why "Try again" always worked: the retry used a fresh connection. Your app's logs showed this exact error with the same reference number as your screenshot.

**Fix:** the gateway now drops unused connections after 4 seconds, well before PostgREST would close them.

**Checks:**
- I sent 440 requests with pauses of up to 61 seconds between batches. Before the fix, 12 failed this way; after it, none did.
- The packaged app passes all 27 smoke checks and all 16 walkthrough checks. Pages open in about 0.2 s typically.

This fix applies to Windows, macOS and Linux. It's pushed to [PR 194](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/194) and the PR description is updated. CI has restarted for the new commit, including the macOS builds that will show whether the earlier Mac fix works. I'm watching it and will report back.

content.text:
Yes, that's right, with three details:

1. **Two ways to run Moneo:**
   - **Not technical:** download the installer from the GitHub Releases page (Windows, Mac or Linux), install it and open it. Nothing else is needed: no Docker, no terminal, no code.
   - **Technical:** download the code and run it with `npm run setup` and `npm run dev`, the same as before.
   - **Phone access through Tailscale works with both.** The downloaded app can also be opened from your phone.

2. **Both use the same code.** A UI change, an AI change or a new page made for the website version also ends up in the app. But app users only get it when you publish a new release and they download and install it again. The app doesn't update itself yet.

3. **Publishing a release is a manual step.** Merging doesn't publish anything. To release:
   - Push a version tag, for example `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.
   - CI then builds all the installers and creates a draft release.
   - You click **Publish** on GitHub.

   The installers aren't code-signed yet. Windows will show a "Windows protected your PC" warning (click More info → Run anyway). On a Mac, the first open needs right-click → Open.

**Merging:** you asked me to merge, so I will, but not yet. GitHub is still blocking it because the checks for the latest commit (the idle-connection fix) are running. I'll merge into `main` as soon as they pass. If any fail, I'll fix that first and won't merge until everything passes.

Everything stays on your computer. There are no accounts and no sign-in screen: one owner, one workspace. The only data that leaves your computer goes to the services you connect (your AI provider, and optionally your bank or Scalable Capital).

## Install

### Desktop preview

Desktop installers are being validated for Windows, macOS and Linux; no desktop release has been published yet. See [desktop setup and operation](desktop/README.md) for packaging, data locations, backups and signing requirements. The desktop app bundles its local backend and does not require Docker or Node.js. The source installation below remains supported.
Scalable questions in chat and voice can combine live holdings, paginated transaction history and transaction details with local JavaScript calculations. The calculation sandbox has no network, filesystem or credentials. Read results remain subject to your AI data scopes and are sent to your configured AI provider as needed to answer. Trades still require accepting an approval card. No additional setup is needed.

### Easiest: let an AI agent install it

If you use an AI coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, it can do the install for you with the `moneo-setup` skill that comes with Moneo. Open the agent in an empty folder and paste:
- Closing the window keeps Moneo in the tray, so background syncs and phone access keep working.
  Quit (tray, Cmd+Q, `Moneo --quit`, OS shutdown) stops the server, then the database, then exits.
- Daily automatic backup while running; Back up now, Open backups folder and Restore from backup in the tray.
- Sign-ins (ChatGPT, banks, Scalable) open in the system browser and return to Moneo's loopback
  callbacks. The callback then opens its result (Import or Settings) in the app window and brings it
  to the front; the browser tab says to continue in Moneo. The server reaches the window through a
  loopback address that is random for each launch and refuses browser requests (`src/auth-return.ts`);
  if the window cannot take it, the browser shows the result as in a source checkout. Every other address also goes to the browser
  (https only). The window allows only the microphone and copying, for Moneo's own pages.

content.text:
I added **App updates** to Settings in the desktop app. It checks for a new release when you click, downloads it, closes Moneo cleanly, installs it and reopens Moneo with all your data. I tested the whole flow on Windows: version 0.1.0 found 0.1.1, updated itself, reopened on its own and still had its data (all 19 checks in the Windows installer test passed).

**How it works:**
- **Check for updates** looks only at releases you've published on GitHub. Drafts are never offered, and Moneo never checks by itself.
- **Update to X** downloads the new version and shows progress. Moneo then closes, installs and reopens by itself; the test update took about 80 seconds.
- **Your data:** it lives outside the app folder, so updates don't touch it. If the new version changes the database, Moneo backs it up first.
- **Windows and Linux (AppImage):** the update installs by itself.
- **Mac and Linux `.deb`:** the button becomes **Download X**, which opens the release page to install by hand. Macs refuse self-updates for apps that aren't code-signed.
- **Phone:** you can't start an update from a phone; it has to be done on the computer running Moneo.
- **Website version:** the section only appears in the desktop app. Source users still update with `git pull`.

**Something went wrong during testing, now fixed:**
- The test copy of Moneo used the same data folder name as your real app.
- One of my timing runs sent it a "quit" command that reached your Moneo and closed it normally (no harm done).
- After the test update, Windows restarted the test copy without the test's settings, so it opened your real data folder for about 8 minutes. It applied no database changes. It only wrote "0.1.1" as the app version in your `config.json`, which corrects itself the next time your own Moneo starts. I shut it down cleanly and restarted your Moneo.
- Test copies now have their own folder ("Moneo QA"), so this can't happen again; the final test run left your Moneo alone.

**Before you can see or use it:**
- The Moneo running on your computer right now is the earlier build without this section.
- Updates only work in the installed app, from a published release. To make one:
  1. Change the version in `desktop/package.json`.
  2. Push a tag such as `v0.1.0`.
  3. Publish the draft release on GitHub.
- Every later release you publish will then show up in **Check for updates**.

**Tests:** lint and type checks pass. In the unit tests, the same 4 time out under full-suite load on this machine and pass when run alone, as before.

## Overview

OpenCode's marketing site is rendered entirely in Berkeley Mono — every word on the page, from the 38px hero headline down to the 14px footer fine print, sits in the same monospaced face. The visual identity comes from that single typographic decision: the page reads like a manpage or a static-site README, complete with bracketed `[+]` / `[-]` / `[x]` ASCII markers used in place of icons or bullets, and a wordmark rendered as block-pixel ASCII art at the top of the nav. There is no sans-serif anywhere, no display face, no italics, no decorative ornament — the system is one font and one weight away from being a 1990s `whatis` page rendered at modern resolutions.

The chrome is austere: warm cream canvas (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc` with a faint blush), nearly-black ink (`{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`), and a 4-tier neutral gray ladder for body, metadata, and disabled text. Cards don't exist as raised surfaces — sections are just hairline-bordered text blocks (`{colors.hairline}` 1px) sitting directly on the canvas with `{spacing.section}` (96px) air between them. The single "visual" moment in the entire system is a full-bleed dark hero card (`{colors.surface-dark}` — true near-black) that mocks up the OpenCode TUI itself: a terminal frame with `tab` / `ctrl-p` keybinding hints, a "Build" command line, and the OpenCode wordmark rendered as a pixel-block ASCII title.

The semantic palette is unusual for a brand-marketing site: it ships the full Apple Human Interface Guidelines accent ramp — `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue `#007aff`), `{colors.danger}` (`#ff3b30`), `{colors.warning}` (`#ff9f0a`), `{colors.success}` (`#30d158`) plus their hover/active deepenings — even though the marketing surfaces themselves only use these colors in the dark hero TUI mockup as syntax-highlight stand-ins. The wider palette belongs to the in-product TUI; the marketing pages mostly stay in monochrome.

**Key Characteristics:**
- 100% Berkeley Mono typography across every text role — no sans-serif fallback anywhere in the chrome
- Warm cream `{colors.canvas}` (#fdfcfc) as the only body background — no surface alternation across sections
- Single dark surface (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #201d1d) reserved exclusively for the hero TUI mockup
- 4px radius (`{rounded.sm}`) on every interactive element; sections themselves are sharp rectangles bordered in 1px hairline
- ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`) used as bullet glyphs in feature lists and FAQ rows
- Block-pixel ASCII wordmark in the primary nav and inside the hero TUI — the brand identity is its own ASCII art
- 96px `{spacing.section}` rhythm between every section, with no decorative dividers; only thin 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules separate content blocks

## Colors

> **Source pages:** `/` (home), `/zen`, `/enterprise`. The chrome palette is identical across all three.

### Brand & Accent
- **Ink** (`{colors.primary}` / `{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`): the brand's only "color." Headlines, body text, primary CTA fill, nav links, and every solid icon. Treats nearly-black as the brand color rather than pure black to keep type readable on the warm cream canvas.
- **Ink Deep** (`{colors.ink-deep}` — `#0f0000`): pressed-state for the primary CTA. Carries a faint red undertone matching the canvas's warm cast.
- **Cream** (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc`): the brand's signature warm white. Used for every page body, every card surface, the on-primary text color, and the ASCII wordmark fill on dark.

### Surface
- **Canvas Cream** (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc`): every page body, every card.
- **Soft Surface** (`{colors.surface-soft}` — `#f8f7f7`): text-input default background, testimonial row fill, alternating row tint.
- **Surface Card** (`{colors.surface-card}` — `#f1eeee`): install-snippet pill, disabled button fill, slightly-elevated section row.
- **Surface Dark** (`{colors.surface-dark}` — `#201d1d`): the hero TUI mockup background and the dark CTA pill on the home page. Identical to `{colors.ink}` — the brand uses one near-black for both text and dark surfaces.
- **Surface Dark Elevated** (`{colors.surface-dark-elevated}` — `#302c2c`): the prompt-row inside the hero TUI mockup, one notch lighter than the dark surface itself.
- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — `rgba(15,0,0,0.12)`): 1px section divider. The translucent warm tint matches the cream canvas's undertone.
- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — `#646262`): tab strip's bottom rule and stronger inline divider.

### Text
- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`): headlines, body text, primary nav links, button text on light surfaces.

The full Apple Human Interface Guidelines semantic ramp ships with the system. On marketing pages these colors appear primarily inside the hero TUI mockup as syntax-highlight stand-ins; in the in-product TUI they carry their conventional meaning.

- **Accent Hover** (`{colors.accent-hover}` — `#0056b3`): pressed informational link.
- **Accent Active** (`{colors.accent-active}` — `#004085`): deeply-pressed informational state.
- **Danger** (`{colors.danger}` — `#ff3b30`): destructive confirmation, error state.
- **Danger Hover** (`{colors.danger-hover}` — `#d70015`): pressed destructive.
- **Danger Active** (`{colors.danger-active}` — `#a50011`): deeply-pressed destructive.
- **Warning** (`{colors.warning}` — `#ff9f0a`): caution callouts.
- **Warning Hover** (`{colors.warning-hover}` — `#cc7f08`): pressed caution.
- **Warning Active** (`{colors.warning-active}` — `#995f06`): deeply-pressed caution.
- **Success** (`{colors.success}` — `#30d158`): positive confirmation, in-TUI success indicator.

## Typography

### Font Family
**Berkeley Mono** is the proprietary monospaced face used across every text role in the system. It carries weights 400 (regular), 500 (medium), and 700 (bold) and falls back through a long monospace stack — IBM Plex Mono → ui-monospace → SFMono-Regular → Menlo → Monaco → Consolas → Liberation Mono → Courier New.

The single-font decision is the brand. There is no display face, no body sans, no italic alternative, and no fallback to a proportional font anywhere — even the legal copyright row uses Berkeley Mono at 14px. This is the most aggressive typographic restraint of any site in the marketing-tools category: OpenCode's identity is "the marketing page is a man page."

### Hierarchy

| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{typography.display-xl}` | 38px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Hero headline ("The open source AI coding agent") |
| `{typography.heading-md}` | 16px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Section label ("What is OpenCode?", "FAQ", "Built for privacy first") |
| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Body copy, paragraph text, list-row text, install-snippet code |
| `{typography.body-strong}` | 16px | 500 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline emphasis, primary nav link, tab-label active |
| `{typography.body-tight}` | 16px | 500 | 1 | 0 | Compact label rendered without breathing room |
| `{typography.link-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline anchor link in body prose |
| `{typography.button-md}` | 16px | 500 | 2 | 0 | Every button label across the system |
| `{typography.caption-md}` | 14px | 400 | 2 | 0 | Footer link text, badge label, copyright row, chart caption |

### Principles
The hierarchy is built almost entirely from size and weight contrast on a single face. The display headline (38px / 700) and the heading-md label (16px / 700) share a weight; the difference is just size. Body and link share size, weight, and line-height — only context distinguishes them. Buttons get a deliberately tall line-height (2.0) so labels feel calmly spaced inside the 4px-radius rectangle.

### Note on Font Substitutes
Berkeley Mono is a paid commercial font. Open-source substitutes that approximate its metrics within ~3% at body sizes:
- **JetBrains Mono** — closest match for stroke contrast and x-height; pair at weights 400 / 500 / 700.
- **IBM Plex Mono** — official secondary fallback in the documented font stack; slightly more open counters but matches line-height behavior.
- **Geist Mono** — modern alternative with similar geometric construction.

When substituting, line-height behavior is preserved by keeping `lineHeight: 1.5` for body and `lineHeight: 2` for buttons — adjusting weight is rarely needed.

## Layout

### Spacing System
- **Base unit:** 8px (with finer 1/2/4px steps available for tight inline gaps).
- **Tokens (front matter):** `{spacing.xxs}` (1px) · `{spacing.xs}` (4px) · `{spacing.sm}` (8px) · `{spacing.md}` (12px) · `{spacing.lg}` (16px) · `{spacing.xl}` (24px) · `{spacing.xxl}` (32px) · `{spacing.section}` (96px).
- **Universal section rhythm:** every page in the set uses `{spacing.section}` (96px) as the vertical gap between major content blocks. This is the largest spacing token in the system and is the dominant layout cue across the home, `/zen`, and `/enterprise` pages.
- **Section internal padding:** content rows inside a section sit at `{spacing.lg}` (16px) vertical with no horizontal padding — text starts flush at the section's left edge.

### Grid & Container
- **Max width:** ~960px content column for body sections; the dark hero TUI mockup is full-bleed within an outer ~1100px content frame.
- **Two-column split:** `/enterprise` pairs a left text block (~360px wide) with a right-aligned form column (~480px wide). The home page is single-column reading.
- **Footer:** 5-up horizontal link row (GitHub / Docs / Changelog / Discord / X) at desktop, collapsing to 2-up at tablet and 1-up at mobile.

### Whitespace Philosophy
Whitespace is structural and generous. Sections sit 96px apart with no decorative dividers between them — the `{colors.hairline}` 1px rule is the only signal of separation. Inside a section, content is left-flush against the column edge with no internal indentation; bullets use ASCII bracket prefixes (`[+]` / `[-]`) instead of indent-based layout. The result is a page that feels like a printed code listing rather than a styled marketing layout.

## Elevation & Depth

| Level | Treatment | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 0 — Flat | No border, no shadow | Default for body sections, list rows, hero text block, footer |
| 1 — Hairline rule | 1px solid `{colors.hairline}` (translucent warm tint) | Section dividers, between major content blocks |
| 2 — Hairline strong | 1px solid `{colors.hairline-strong}` | Tab strip bottom rule, in-list emphasized divider |
| 3 — Inverted dark | `{colors.surface-dark}` fill | Hero TUI mockup, dark CTA pill — the system's only "elevated" surface uses color, not shadow |

There are no drop shadows in the system. Nothing lifts, nothing floats. The only way an element registers as "above" another is the dark surface used in the hero mockup.

### Decorative Depth
Depth comes from typography density and the single dark TUI mockup, not from CSS effects:
- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** — the OpenCode brand name rendered as a 5-row block of monospaced character cells, used in the primary nav and as the centerpiece of the hero TUI mockup.
- **Hero TUI mockup** — full-bleed `{colors.surface-dark}` rectangle containing a faux terminal interface: ASCII wordmark, a `tui-prompt-row` showing a Build command line, and `tab switch agent` / `ctrl-p commands` keybinding hints in `{colors.ash}` at the bottom edge.
- **Chart tiles** — three thin-line ASCII charts inside the home page's "open source AI coding agent" stat block, with abstract dotted/sparse-line plots in `{colors.body}` against the cream canvas. Captions sit beneath in `{typography.caption-md}` (`Fig 1. 150K GitHub Stars`, `Fig 2. 850 Contributors`, `Fig 3. 6.5M Monthly Devs`).

## Shapes

### Border Radius Scale

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Sections, hero TUI mockup, primary nav, footer, list rows — every container that isn't a button |
| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Every interactive element — primary CTA, secondary CTA, text inputs, install snippet, badges, prompt rows |
| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Avatar circles in testimonials |

The radius vocabulary is two values: 4px for interactive elements and 0px for everything else. Avatar circles in testimonial rows are the only fully-rounded element in the system.

### Photography Geometry
There is no photography. Visual elements are limited to:
- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** in the nav and hero TUI mockup.
- **Inline ASCII charts** inside the stat-block section — abstract sparse-line and dotted plots without specific data points.
- **Avatar dots** (~32px) inside testimonial rows on `/zen` — flat colored circles in `{rounded.full}`.
- **In-product icons** (kbd, A+, ⊕, ↻, K, Z) rendered as small monospaced character glyphs, not bitmaps or SVG.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Render every text role in Berkeley Mono. The single-font decision is the entire identity.
- Keep `{colors.canvas}` (`#fdfcfc`) as the only body background. Don't introduce gray section bands.
- Use ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`, `+`, `−`) as bullets, toggles, and section glyphs. They are the brand's only iconography.
- Anchor the dark `{component.hero-tui-mockup}` exactly once per landing page as the hero centerpiece. Never use the dark surface for body content.
- Reserve `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue) and the rest of the semantic ramp for in-TUI states; marketing chrome stays monochrome.
- Use `{rounded.sm}` (4px) on every interactive element and `{rounded.none}` (0px) on every container.
- Stack content sections at `{spacing.section}` (96px) rhythm with only 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules between them.

### Don't
- Don't introduce a sans-serif body font, a display face, or an italic style. Berkeley Mono carries everything.
- Don't add drop shadows, gradients, or atmospheric backgrounds. The system is flat-on-cream.
- Don't replace the ASCII bracket markers with SVG icons. The brackets are the icons.
- Don't use the semantic accent ramp (`{colors.accent}`, `{colors.warning}`, `{colors.danger}`, `{colors.success}`) on marketing CTAs. They belong to the in-product TUI.

223	## Overview
224	
225	OpenCode's marketing site is rendered entirely in Berkeley Mono — every word on the page, from the 38px hero headline down to the 14px footer fine print, sits in the same monospaced face. The visual identity comes from that single typographic decision: the page reads like a manpage or a static-site README, complete with bracketed `[+]` / `[-]` / `[x]` ASCII markers used in place of icons or bullets, and a wordmark rendered as block-pixel ASCII art at the top of the nav. There is no sans-serif anywhere, no display face, no italics, no decorative ornament — the system is one font and one weight away from being a 1990s `whatis` page rendered at modern resolutions.
226	
227	The chrome is austere: warm cream canvas (`{colors.canvas}` — `#fdfcfc` with a faint blush), nearly-black ink (`{colors.ink}` — `#201d1d`), and a 4-tier neutral gray ladder for body, metadata, and disabled text. Cards don't exist as raised surfaces — sections are just hairline-bordered text blocks (`{colors.hairline}` 1px) sitting directly on the canvas with `{spacing.section}` (96px) air between them. The single "visual" moment in the entire system is a full-bleed dark hero card (`{colors.surface-dark}` — true near-black) that mocks up the OpenCode TUI itself: a terminal frame with `tab` / `ctrl-p` keybinding hints, a "Build" command line, and the OpenCode wordmark rendered as a pixel-block ASCII title.
228	
229	The semantic palette is unusual for a brand-marketing site: it ships the full Apple Human Interface Guidelines accent ramp — `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue `#007aff`), `{colors.danger}` (`#ff3b30`), `{colors.warning}` (`#ff9f0a`), `{colors.success}` (`#30d158`) plus their hover/active deepenings — even though the marketing surfaces themselves only use these colors in the dark hero TUI mockup as syntax-highlight stand-ins. The wider palette belongs to the in-product TUI; the marketing pages mostly stay in monochrome.
230	
231	**Key Characteristics:**
232	- 100% Berkeley Mono typography across every text role — no sans-serif fallback anywhere in the chrome
233	- Warm cream `{colors.canvas}` (#fdfcfc) as the only body background — no surface alternation across sections
234	- Single dark surface (`{colors.surface-dark}` — #201d1d) reserved exclusively for the hero TUI mockup
235	- 4px radius (`{rounded.sm}`) on every interactive element; sections themselves are sharp rectangles bordered in 1px hairline
236	- ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`) used as bullet glyphs in feature lists and FAQ rows
237	- Block-pixel ASCII wordmark in the primary nav and inside the hero TUI — the brand identity is its own ASCII art
238	- 96px `{spacing.section}` rhythm between every section, with no decorative dividers; only thin 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules separate content blocks

280	## Typography
281	
282	### Font Family
283	**Berkeley Mono** is the proprietary monospaced face used across every text role in the system. It carries weights 400 (regular), 500 (medium), and 700 (bold) and falls back through a long monospace stack — IBM Plex Mono → ui-monospace → SFMono-Regular → Menlo → Monaco → Consolas → Liberation Mono → Courier New.
284	
285	The single-font decision is the brand. There is no display face, no body sans, no italic alternative, and no fallback to a proportional font anywhere — even the legal copyright row uses Berkeley Mono at 14px. This is the most aggressive typographic restraint of any site in the marketing-tools category: OpenCode's identity is "the marketing page is a man page."
286	
287	### Hierarchy
288	
289	| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
290	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
291	| `{typography.display-xl}` | 38px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Hero headline ("The open source AI coding agent") |
292	| `{typography.heading-md}` | 16px | 700 | 1.5 | 0 | Section label ("What is OpenCode?", "FAQ", "Built for privacy first") |
293	| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Body copy, paragraph text, list-row text, install-snippet code |
294	| `{typography.body-strong}` | 16px | 500 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline emphasis, primary nav link, tab-label active |
295	| `{typography.body-tight}` | 16px | 500 | 1 | 0 | Compact label rendered without breathing room |
296	| `{typography.link-md}` | 16px | 400 | 1.5 | 0 | Inline anchor link in body prose |
297	| `{typography.button-md}` | 16px | 500 | 2 | 0 | Every button label across the system |
298	| `{typography.caption-md}` | 14px | 400 | 2 | 0 | Footer link text, badge label, copyright row, chart caption |
299	
300	### Principles
301	The hierarchy is built almost entirely from size and weight contrast on a single face. The display headline (38px / 700) and the heading-md label (16px / 700) share a weight; the difference is just size. Body and link share size, weight, and line-height — only context distinguishes them. Buttons get a deliberately tall line-height (2.0) so labels feel calmly spaced inside the 4px-radius rectangle.
302	
303	### Note on Font Substitutes
304	Berkeley Mono is a paid commercial font. Open-source substitutes that approximate its metrics within ~3% at body sizes:
305	- **JetBrains Mono** — closest match for stroke contrast and x-height; pair at weights 400 / 500 / 700.
306	- **IBM Plex Mono** — official secondary fallback in the documented font stack; slightly more open counters but matches line-height behavior.
307	- **Geist Mono** — modern alternative with similar geometric construction.
308	
309	When substituting, line-height behavior is preserved by keeping `lineHeight: 1.5` for body and `lineHeight: 2` for buttons — adjusting weight is rarely needed.
310	
311	## Layout
312	
313	### Spacing System
314	- **Base unit:** 8px (with finer 1/2/4px steps available for tight inline gaps).
315	- **Tokens (front matter):** `{spacing.xxs}` (1px) · `{spacing.xs}` (4px) · `{spacing.sm}` (8px) · `{spacing.md}` (12px) · `{spacing.lg}` (16px) · `{spacing.xl}` (24px) · `{spacing.xxl}` (32px) · `{spacing.section}` (96px).
316	- **Universal section rhythm:** every page in the set uses `{spacing.section}` (96px) as the vertical gap between major content blocks. This is the largest spacing token in the system and is the dominant layout cue across the home, `/zen`, and `/enterprise` pages.
317	- **Section internal padding:** content rows inside a section sit at `{spacing.lg}` (16px) vertical with no horizontal padding — text starts flush at the section's left edge.
318	
319	### Grid & Container
320	- **Max width:** ~960px content column for body sections; the dark hero TUI mockup is full-bleed within an outer ~1100px content frame.
321	- **Two-column split:** `/enterprise` pairs a left text block (~360px wide) with a right-aligned form column (~480px wide). The home page is single-column reading.
322	- **Footer:** 5-up horizontal link row (GitHub / Docs / Changelog / Discord / X) at desktop, collapsing to 2-up at tablet and 1-up at mobile.
323	
324	### Whitespace Philosophy
325	Whitespace is structural and generous. Sections sit 96px apart with no decorative dividers between them — the `{colors.hairline}` 1px rule is the only signal of separation. Inside a section, content is left-flush against the column edge with no internal indentation; bullets use ASCII bracket prefixes (`[+]` / `[-]`) instead of indent-based layout. The result is a page that feels like a printed code listing rather than a styled marketing layout.
326	
327	## Elevation & Depth
328	
329	| Level | Treatment | Use |
330	|---|---|---|
331	| 0 — Flat | No border, no shadow | Default for body sections, list rows, hero text block, footer |
332	| 1 — Hairline rule | 1px solid `{colors.hairline}` (translucent warm tint) | Section dividers, between major content blocks |
333	| 2 — Hairline strong | 1px solid `{colors.hairline-strong}` | Tab strip bottom rule, in-list emphasized divider |
334	| 3 — Inverted dark | `{colors.surface-dark}` fill | Hero TUI mockup, dark CTA pill — the system's only "elevated" surface uses color, not shadow |
335	
336	There are no drop shadows in the system. Nothing lifts, nothing floats. The only way an element registers as "above" another is the dark surface used in the hero mockup.
337	
338	### Decorative Depth
339	Depth comes from typography density and the single dark TUI mockup, not from CSS effects:
340	- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** — the OpenCode brand name rendered as a 5-row block of monospaced character cells, used in the primary nav and as the centerpiece of the hero TUI mockup.
341	- **Hero TUI mockup** — full-bleed `{colors.surface-dark}` rectangle containing a faux terminal interface: ASCII wordmark, a `tui-prompt-row` showing a Build command line, and `tab switch agent` / `ctrl-p commands` keybinding hints in `{colors.ash}` at the bottom edge.
342	- **Chart tiles** — three thin-line ASCII charts inside the home page's "open source AI coding agent" stat block, with abstract dotted/sparse-line plots in `{colors.body}` against the cream canvas. Captions sit beneath in `{typography.caption-md}` (`Fig 1. 150K GitHub Stars`, `Fig 2. 850 Contributors`, `Fig 3. 6.5M Monthly Devs`).
343	
344	## Shapes
345	
346	### Border Radius Scale
347	
348	| Token | Value | Use |
349	|---|---|---|
350	| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Sections, hero TUI mockup, primary nav, footer, list rows — every container that isn't a button |
351	| `{rounded.sm}` | 4px | Every interactive element — primary CTA, secondary CTA, text inputs, install snippet, badges, prompt rows |
352	| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Avatar circles in testimonials |
353	
354	The radius vocabulary is two values: 4px for interactive elements and 0px for everything else. Avatar circles in testimonial rows are the only fully-rounded element in the system.
355	
356	### Photography Geometry
357	There is no photography. Visual elements are limited to:
358	- **ASCII block-pixel wordmark** in the nav and hero TUI mockup.
359	- **Inline ASCII charts** inside the stat-block section — abstract sparse-line and dotted plots without specific data points.
360	- **Avatar dots** (~32px) inside testimonial rows on `/zen` — flat colored circles in `{rounded.full}`.
361	- **In-product icons** (kbd, A+, ⊕, ↻, K, Z) rendered as small monospaced character glyphs, not bitmaps or SVG.

414	- Container: full-bleed `{colors.surface-dark}` (~near-black), padding `64px 32px`, rounded `{rounded.none}`.

423	- Each row begins with a `[+]` / `[-]` / `[x]` ASCII marker followed by a bold label and a regular description: e.g., `[+] LSP enabled    Automatically loads the right LSPs for the IDE`. The bracket marker is part of the text content, not a separate icon.

457	
458	## Do's and Don'ts
459	
460	### Do
461	- Render every text role in Berkeley Mono. The single-font decision is the entire identity.
462	- Keep `{colors.canvas}` (`#fdfcfc`) as the only body background. Don't introduce gray section bands.
463	- Use ASCII bracket markers (`[+]`, `[-]`, `[x]`, `+`, `−`) as bullets, toggles, and section glyphs. They are the brand's only iconography.
464	- Anchor the dark `{component.hero-tui-mockup}` exactly once per landing page as the hero centerpiece. Never use the dark surface for body content.
465	- Reserve `{colors.accent}` (Apple Blue) and the rest of the semantic ramp for in-TUI states; marketing chrome stays monochrome.
466	- Use `{rounded.sm}` (4px) on every interactive element and `{rounded.none}` (0px) on every container.
467	- Stack content sections at `{spacing.section}` (96px) rhythm with only 1px `{colors.hairline}` rules between them.
468	
469	### Don't
470	- Don't introduce a sans-serif body font, a display face, or an italic style. Berkeley Mono carries everything.
471	- Don't add drop shadows, gradients, or atmospheric backgrounds. The system is flat-on-cream.
472	- Don't replace the ASCII bracket markers with SVG icons. The brackets are the icons.
473	- Don't use the semantic accent ramp (`{colors.accent}`, `{colors.warning}`, `{colors.danger}`, `{colors.success}`) on marketing CTAs. They belong to the in-product TUI.
474	- Don't pad cards with 24px+ internal padding. List rows sit at 8px vertical; FAQ rows at 12px.
475	- Don't render the OpenCode wordmark as a vector logo. It is always block-pixel ASCII.
476	- Don't fill the hero TUI mockup with photography or illustration. It is text-only and always shows a faux terminal command line.
477	
478	## Responsive Behavior
479	
480	### Breakpoints
481	
482	| Name | Width | Key Changes |
483	|---|---|---|
484	| desktop-large | 1280px+ | Default — 960px content column, 5-up footer link grid |
485	| desktop | 1024px | Same layout; nav remains horizontal |
486	| tablet | 850px | Footer collapses to 2-up grid; `/enterprise` two-column form stacks |
487	| tablet-narrow | 768px | Primary nav becomes hamburger drawer; Download CTA stays visible |
488	| mobile | 640px | Single-column everything; hero display drops 38px → ~28px; section padding tightens |
489	
490	### Touch Targets
491	All interactive elements meet WCAG AA at the ~36–40px height range. `{component.button-primary}` sits at ~36px with 20px horizontal padding. `{component.text-input}` and `{component.textarea}` sit at ~40px. `{component.button-tab}` rows in the install-method strip sit at ~32–36px depending on label length but extend to a full 44px tappable cell via inline padding. Footer links use `{typography.caption-md}` (14px) but receive ~28px line-height (caption-md is 2.0) plus 8px vertical padding for a comfortable ~44px tappable row.
492	
493	### Collapsing Strategy
494	- **Primary nav:** desktop horizontal cluster → tablet-narrow hamburger drawer at 768px. The dark "Download" CTA stays visible at all widths.
495	- **Hero TUI mockup:** maintains its full-bleed dark surface at every breakpoint; the ASCII wordmark scales proportionally and the keybinding-hint row may wrap to two lines on narrow screens.
496	- **Install snippet + tab strip:** desktop fixed-width pill → mobile full-width pill with horizontal scroll on the tab strip if labels overflow.
497	- **Footer:** 5-up horizontal link grid → 2-up at tablet → 1-up at mobile (each link becomes a full-width row).
498	- **`/enterprise` two-column layout:** desktop 50/50 → tablet stacks to single-column with the form below the text block.
499	- **Section padding:** `{spacing.section}` (96px) desktop → 64px tablet → 48px mobile.
500	- **Hero headline:** `{typography.display-xl}` (38px) at desktop, scaling to ~28px at mobile, line-height holding at 1.5.
501	
502	### Image Behavior
503	There are no raster images in the system aside from the favicon and OG share image. Every visual element — wordmarks, charts, icons — is rendered as type or inline SVG and scales without aspect-ratio considerations.
504	
505	## Iteration Guide
506	
507	1. Focus on ONE component at a time. Pull its YAML entry and verify every property resolves.
508	2. Reference component names and tokens directly (`{colors.ink}`, `{component.hero-tui-mockup}`, `{rounded.sm}`) — do not paraphrase.
509	3. Run `npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md` after edits — `broken-ref`, `contrast-ratio`, and `orphaned-tokens` warnings flag issues automatically.
510	4. Add new variants as separate component entries (`-active`, `-disabled`) — do not bury them inside prose.
511	5. Default body to `{typography.body-md}`; reach for `{typography.body-strong}` for emphasis; reserve `{typography.display-xl}` strictly for the page-top hero headline.
512	6. Keep `{colors.surface-dark}` scarce — at most one full-bleed dark mockup per page. The dark surface is a narrative device, not a chrome treatment.
513	7. When introducing a new component, ask whether it can be expressed with the existing ASCII-bracket + 4px-radius + Berkeley-Mono vocabulary before adding new tokens. The system's strength is that it almost never needs new ones.
514	
515	## Known Gaps
516	
517	- **Mobile screenshots not captured** — responsive behavior synthesizes OpenCode's mobile pattern (hamburger drawer, single-column, footer accordion) from desktop evidence and the breakpoint stack.
518	- **Hover states not documented** by system policy.
519	- **In-product TUI screenshots** beyond the marketing hero mockup are not in the captured set; the actual `opencode` terminal interface (full keybindings, panels, status bar) is not documented here.

521	- **Form validation state styling** (success / error inline messages) not present in the captured surfaces.

New Moneo Desktop: no Docker, no terminal. Download →

Personal finance that runs
on your own computer.

Moneo imports your statements, syncs your bank and investments, tracks your net worth and answers questions about your money. Everything stays on your machine. It's open source, so you can read every line.

↓ Download Moneo View the source

Windows · macOS · Linux · MIT licensed

Ask You spent €412.60 on groceries so far in November, €37.90 less than by this date in October.

ctrl k search or askg w wealthg i import

What is Moneo?

One private workspace for your money, with no account to create and nothing to host.

  • [+]Import statementsCSV and PDF statements from any bank, with a review step and undo for every import.
  • [+]Sync your bankConnect European banks through Enable Banking. Balances and transactions stay up to date.
  • [+]Track investmentsScalable Capital holdings and history, plus assets and debts you add yourself.
  • [+]See your net worthEvery account, asset and debt in one number, with its history.
  • [+]Plan aheadRecurring payments, spending plans and a forecast of where your balance is heading.
  • [+]Ask about your moneyChat or talk to an AI that reads your real numbers. Any change it suggests waits for you to accept it.
  • [+]Use it on your phoneOpen it from your own phone and tablet over private Tailscale, and install it like an app.

Two ways to run it

Same app, same features. Pick whichever suits you. Changes to the code reach both.

  • [1]Download Moneo for your computer below and install it.
  • [2]Open it. The first start creates your private database, which takes about a minute.
  • [3]Add your AI key or sign in with ChatGPT in Settings, then import a statement or connect a bank.

For people who just want to use it: no Docker, Node.js or terminal needed. Updates come from Settings → App updates.

git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
npm run setup   # starts the backend in Docker, creates your login
npm start       # http://localhost:3000

For developers: needs Node.js 22 and Docker. Change anything you like; the README covers setup, phone access and updates.

Download

Looking up the latest release…

WindowsWindows 10 and 11 · 64-bit installer macOS · Apple siliconM1 and newer · .dmg macOS · IntelIntel Macs · .dmg Linux · AppImageMost distributions · updates itself Linux · .debDebian and Ubuntu
Your computer may warn you the first time

The installers aren't code-signed yet, so your system doesn't know the publisher. You can check each file against SHA256SUMS.txt in the release.

  • Windows: if “Windows protected your PC” appears, choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • macOS: right-click Moneo in Applications, choose Open, then Open again.
  • Linux AppImage: make it executable (chmod +x Moneo-*.AppImage), then run it.

Built for privacy first

  • [x]No account, no cloudMoneo runs on your computer and answers only on it. There is no Moneo server and no sign-up.
  • [x]Data leaves only where you send itYour AI provider, and your bank or Scalable if you connect them. Nothing else, and no analytics.
  • [x]Numbers come from codeMoney is stored exactly in your currency. The AI explains and proposes; it never quietly changes your data.
  • [x]History is keptImports, corrections and changes can be undone, and the app backs up your data every day.
  • [x]Open sourceMIT licensed. Read the code, change it, run your own build.

FAQ

Is Moneo free?

Yes. Moneo is free and open source under the MIT license. The AI uses your own ChatGPT plan or an API key, so any AI costs are between you and your provider.

Does any of my financial data go online?

Only to services you connect yourself: the AI provider when you ask a question, Enable Banking to sync your bank, and Scalable Capital for investments. Everything else stays in the database on your computer.

What's the difference between the app and running from source?

None in features. The app bundles everything (database included), so you just install it. Running from source is for people who want to change the code; it uses Docker for the database.

Can I use it on my phone?

Yes. Turn on phone access in Settings and connect your phone with Tailscale, a free private network for your own devices. Moneo stays on your computer; your phone opens it from there.

How do updates work?

In the app, open Settings → App updates and choose Check for updates. On Windows and Linux (AppImage) Moneo installs the update and restarts with your data. On a Mac it opens the download. From source, run git pull and npm run setup.

Which banks work?

Banks available through Enable Banking, which covers many banks across Europe. Any bank works through statement import.

If you already downloaded Moneo, open the agent in the Moneo folder and say **"set up Moneo"**. The agent runs the commands, tells you what each step does, and asks you only for what it can't do itself, like installing Docker or entering your keys in Moneo. If it can control your browser or computer, it asks first and then does the clicking too. You type passwords and keys yourself.

### Or install it yourself

#### 1. Install the tools

- [Git](https://git-scm.com/downloads)
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) version 22 or newer
- [Docker Desktop](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) (on Linux, Docker Engine with Compose)

Start Docker Desktop and wait until it says it is running.

#### 2. Download Moneo

```sh
git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
```

#### 3. Run the setup

```sh
npm run setup
```

This creates the database in Docker, makes all the passwords and secrets Moneo needs, and saves them in a file called `.env`. The first run downloads a few GB and takes several minutes; you need about 4 GB of free disk space. On Windows a security prompt may ask to install a local certificate: click **Yes** (it is only used for bank connections and only trusted on this computer).

You never need to open or edit `.env`. Keep it private and don't delete it.

#### 4. Start Moneo

```sh
npm run build
npm start
```

The build takes a few minutes the first time. Then open **http://localhost:3000**.

#### 5. Turn on the AI

Go to **Settings → Keys and connections → AI access** and choose one:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** to use your ChatGPT Go, Plus or Pro plan, or
- **Paste an OpenAI API key** ([create one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)) and click **Save key**. Usage is billed to that key.

Voice calls and dictation need the OpenAI API key. An OpenRouter key is optional (for other models).

#### 6. Add your money

- **Import** a CSV or Excel export from your bank, or
- connect your bank or Scalable Capital (optional, see below).

That's it. Want it on your phone or tablet too? See [Use it from your phone or tablet](#use-it-from-your-phone-or-tablet-optional).

## Everyday use

- **Start Moneo:** `npm start` in the Moneo folder (Docker Desktop must be running).
- **Stop Moneo:** press `Ctrl+C`. The database keeps running in Docker; `docker compose stop` stops it.
- **Update Moneo:**
  ```sh
  git pull
  npm ci
  npm run setup
  npm run build
  npm start
  ```
  Your data and secrets are kept.

While Moneo runs it does its background work by itself: scheduled summaries, and syncing your bank and Scalable about once a day. Anything missed while your computer was off runs shortly after you start Moneo.

Skip to content
Moneo
Features Get it Privacy FAQ GitHub
Download

New Moneo Desktop: just install and open it. Download →

Your money, on your computer.
Not someone else's server.

Moneo shows your net worth, syncs your bank and investments, plans what's coming and answers questions about your money. It's open source and runs entirely on your own machine.

↓ Download Moneo View the source on GitHub

Free · Windows, macOS, Linux · MIT licensed

Sample data. Your own numbers never leave your computer.

What it does

Everything about your money, in one private place

Ask

Ask about your money in plain words

“Where did my money go in October?” Moneo reads your real transactions and answers with the numbers, tables and charts. Call it and talk instead of typing. Any change it suggests waits for you to accept it.

  • Uses your ChatGPT plan or your own API key
  • You choose which data the AI may see

Artifacts

Build your own pages and reports

Describe the page you want, like a monthly money story, a subscription radar or a goals tracker, and Moneo builds it from your data. Keep it, refine it in chat, and pin it to your Home as a card.

  • Always shows your latest numbers
  • Runs in a sandbox with no internet access

Wealth

Your net worth, traced

Bank accounts, Scalable Capital investments, and assets and debts you add yourself, in one number with its history. Moneo shows where every change came from.

  • Bank sync through Enable Banking (Europe)
  • Or import CSV and Excel statements, with undo

Plan

See what's coming before it happens

Moneo finds your recurring payments, forecasts your cash for the next weeks and months, and tracks spending plans and savings goals.

  • Conservative and optimistic range
  • Try “what if” scenarios safely

Phone

On your phone too, still private

Turn on phone access and open Moneo from your own phone and tablet over Tailscale, a free private network for your devices. Add it to your home screen like an app. Your data stays on your computer.

Get it

Two ways to run it

Same app, same features. Changes to the code reach both.

Download the app

For everyone. Install it and open it: no Docker, Node.js or terminal. Updates come from Settings → App updates.

  1. Download Moneo for your computer below.
  2. Open it. The first start sets up your private database (about a minute).
  3. Add your AI in Settings, then import a statement or connect your bank.
↓ Download

Run from the source

For developers who want to read or change the code. Needs Git, Node.js 22 or newer and Docker.

git clone https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo.git
cd Moneo
npm ci
npm run setup
npm run build
npm start
Read the setup guide

Download

Get Moneo for your computer

Looking up the latest release…

WindowsWindows 10 and 11, 64-bit macOS, Apple siliconM1 and newer macOS, IntelIntel Macs Linux AppImageMost distributions, updates itself Linux .debDebian and Ubuntu
Your computer may warn you the first time

The installers aren't code-signed yet, so your system doesn't recognise the publisher. You can check each file against SHA256SUMS.txt in the release.

  • Windows: if “Windows protected your PC” appears, choose More info, then Run anyway.
  • macOS: right-click Moneo in Applications, choose Open, then Open again.
  • Linux AppImage: make it executable (chmod +x Moneo-*.AppImage), then run it.

Privacy

Built so your data stays yours

No account, no cloud

Moneo runs on your computer. There is no Moneo server and no sign-up.

Only what you connect

Data goes only to your AI provider, and your bank or Scalable if you connect them. No analytics, no tracking.

Numbers come from code

Money is stored exactly, in its currency. The AI explains and proposes; it never quietly changes your data.

Nothing is lost

Imports and changes can be undone, and the desktop app backs up your data every day.

FAQ

Questions

Is Moneo free?

Yes. Moneo is free and open source under the MIT license. The AI uses your own ChatGPT plan or an API key, so any AI costs are between you and your provider.

Does any of my financial data go online?

Only to services you connect yourself: your AI provider when you ask a question, Enable Banking to sync your bank, and Scalable Capital for investments. Everything else stays in the database on your computer.

What's the difference between the app and running from source?

None in features. The app bundles everything, the database included, so you just install it. Running from source is for people who want to change the code; it uses Docker for the database.

Can I use it on my phone?

Yes. Turn on phone access in Settings and connect your phone with Tailscale. Moneo stays on your computer; your phone opens it from there.

How do updates work?

In the app, open Settings → App updates and choose Check for updates. On Windows and Linux (AppImage) Moneo installs the update and restarts with your data. On a Mac it opens the download. From source: git pull, npm ci, npm run setup, npm run build, then npm start.

Which banks work?

Banks available through Enable Banking, which covers many banks across Europe. Any bank works through statement import.

Take your finances back home.

↓ Download Moneo Star on GitHub

GitHub Releases Docs Issues Privacy Terms
MIT license
